name: Seasonal work permit, Type S (zezwolenie na pracę sezonową)

requirements.blocker_text: Work must fall within one of the government-designated seasonal PKD business-activity subclasses -- primarily agriculture, horticulture, animal husbandry, accommodation, and catering.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the offered role sits within a designated seasonal PKD subclass, or apply for a different work route if not.

requirements.blocker_text: The Polish employer applies to the starosta (district authority, not the voivode) for the permit before work begins, and pays a PLN 30 filing fee.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a seasonal job offer from a Polish employer willing to file the Type S application.

requirements.blocker_text: Wage terms must match those of comparable Polish workers and cannot fall below the statutory minimum wage.
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate a wage at or above the statutory minimum.

evidence_required.document: Written employment contract in a language the worker understands

outcome.duration_length: up to 9 months within a calendar year
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: max 9 months per calendar year on this status; does not accumulate toward permanent residence or citizenship

sources.title: Ministerstwo Rodziny, Pracy i Polityki Społecznej (praca.gov.pl portal) -- Zezwolenia na pracę sezonową
Państwowa Inspekcja Pracy (National Labour Inspectorate) -- Praca sezonowa cudzoziemców na terytorium Polski, corroborating the PKD sector list and PLN 30 filing fee
biznes.gov.pl (official Polish government business portal) -- Uzyskaj zezwolenie na pracę sezonową, corroborating the 9-month cap and multi-season registration mechanics

notes: Structurally a dead-end route by design: seasonal work explicitly does not count toward permanent residence or citizenship timelines (physical_presence_requirement note), and the government's own declaration-procedure (oświadczenie) page explicitly states seasonal work cannot be authorised via that simplified channel either -- Type S is a closed, separate system, confirmed via pip.gov.pl (National Labour Inspectorate). Citizens of Armenia, Belarus, Moldova, and Ukraine get one enhancement unavailable to others: a multi-season entry allowing a single registration to cover up to 9 months per year across up to 3 consecutive calendar years, provided the employer has hired that same worker under a Type S permit at least once in the preceding 5 years -- a genuine structural nuance not modeled as a separate requirement_group here since it only changes the administrative registration mechanism, not the underlying eligibility test, but worth flagging for anyone building the UI's blocker/fix-path display for this route. leads_to_pr and leads_to_citizenship are correctly false, not merely unpopulated -- this is one of the few routes across the whole 214-route dataset (Poland's 15th country) that is a genuine structural dead-end by government design, similar in shape to how visit-category routes work elsewhere, despite being classified as work_sponsored rather than visit.
